text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - The UK stock market hit record highs on Tuesday but ended on a subdued note after Wall Street failed to live up to a promising start. The FTSE 100 index, underpinned by soaring sterling, firm gilts and Wall Street's record close overnight, had reached a record 4,063.2 points earlier in the day and looked poised for further gains as the U.S. market was tipped to open higher. But late-afternoon dealing saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average pare its initial 34-point gain and the FTSE, suspicious of the U.S. market's stamina, slipped to end the day off highs at a record close of 4,050.8, up 12.1 points.

FRANKFURT- Germany's DAX index, which measures trade in 30 blue-chip German shares, closed bourse dealings at an all-time record closing high after Wall Street strength overnight, a firmer dollar and bond gains. The DAX closed up 34.57 points at 2,728.45, after briefly touching 2,728.64. In post bourse trade the Dax stood at 2,718.73 up 17.90 points.

PARIS - French shares closed at a closing high for the year but off their best levels on Tuesday, after a rally on the back of Wall Street's bull run, traders said. Alcatel fell sharply in late trading on market talk it had won the bidding for electronics group Thomson but the missiles activities were being sold to Lagardere, traders said. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 24.66 points at 2,168.28.

ZURICH - Swiss shares closed at a record high despite profit taking that undermined midday all-time highs above 3,838 points on the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI). Sentiment was good given Wall Street's record run and a strong U.S. dollar, dealers said. The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) added 5.37 points to 2,446.25 points.

TOKYO - Stocks surged in the trading session, pushed by new record highs on Wall Street overnight as well as speculation that the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) may win a majority in the Lower House of parliament in Japan's general election on Sunday. The benchmark Nikkei 225 jumped 400.68 points to close at 21,429.93.

HONG KONG - The Hang Seng index recorded its third record closing high in under a week, driven higher by continued interest in property and banking stocks. The Hang Seng index closed the session at a record 12,490.70, up 160.35 points. Turnover was HK$8.41 billion.

SYDNEY - A Dow-inspired share market ended at its second-straight record close although early gains were nearly wiped-out late in the session by profit-taking and a fall in the shares of Rupert Murdoch's international media company, News Corp. The key All Ordinaries index closed 2.9 points higher at 2,366.2, well off its intra-day and life-time high of 2,380.8.

JOHANNESBURG - The South African all-share index ended at a record high for the second day running, but hugged Monday's levels as the market lost steam during the day. Golds eased on a dull bullion price. Dealers said there was general disappointment that the market failed to ride further on the back of strong world markets, some of which also set record highs. The market was seen carrying on better during the week and the U.S. CPI figure due on Wednesday would provide direction, dealers said. The overall index ended up 1.6 points to 7,073.1 points, golds gained 7.7 points to 8,306 points and golds were down 11.7 points to 1,723.5 points.
